name: hibernate
title: Hibernate — far more sessions than fit in RAM
summary: Millions of ECMAScript sessions, a few percent resident: the host unloads idle ones to a blob file and brings them back on demand.
description: Spawns ECMAScript session actors (a set of ids, a small profile, a timeout as a delayed send to itself) far beyond what fits resident, while the host sweeps for cold actors (ta_system_cold_actors, a CLOCK sweep) and hibernates them into an append-only blob file. Touches are skewed: most go to a small hot set, the rest to random sessions, which are hibernated and must be woken first — the system queues their events and emits TA_EFFECT_WAKE, the host reads the blob and calls ta_actor_wake. A sample of touches replies, measuring hot vs cold latency. Hibernated sessions keep their actor record (session address, timers, mailbox); their state lives in the file. Tune with --param sessions, hotFraction, hotShare, touchRate, sweepMs, idleMs.
